board: Probe Cube (STM32 Nucleo-H723ZG, Nautilus UART LAB)
notes: Each component is assigned its own lab port (see Probe cube status). Every board API runs on that port; {port} is filled in for you.
A cfg the board rejects is reported with ok=false and the console reply. If it was a port-level failure, the backend restores the last good config (restored_config).

Failure signatures: notices with '0x00 suppressed' = gross baud mismatch or RX held low; no data at all = loose wire or sensor not transmitting; garbled lines / junk bytes + FE = wrong baud or framing; PE = parity mismatch.

Sampling results include link counter deltas for the port (rx, ORE, FE, NE, PE, zeros, dropped), the measured rate_hz, seq_gaps (missed frames, when the sensor numbers them), garbled_lines and, for binary sensors, decoder stats (checksum_errors, junk_bytes). Error counters count polls, not bytes: read them as zero vs climbing.

ports.description: List every lab port: open/closed, configured and actual baud, framing and link counters (look at the component's own port).

set_baud.description: Set the baud rate of the lab port the sensor is on.

set_data_bits.description: Set the number of data bits (excluding parity) of the lab port.

set_parity.description: Set the parity of the lab port.

set_stop_bits.description: Set the number of stop bits of the lab port.

clear_counters.description: Zero the lab port's RX/TX and error counters.

stream_probe.description: Listen to the sensor for a few seconds and report valid readings: count, measured rate_hz, the last values, decoder stats (checksum_errors, junk_bytes) and notices. Starts/stops the stream if the sensor needs it. Use it to prove the link for sensors that never acknowledge commands.

seconds.description: Listening time, 0.5-10 (default 2, or the sensor's probe_seconds for slow sensors)
